children: ChangXin Memory Technologies has ridden the artificial-intelligence boom to become China's most valuable company-and soaring revenue may help power shares even higher next week.

The memory-chip maker filed its first earnings report since going public in July on Friday. For the first half of 2026, it posted net income of 117.1 billion yuan ($17.4 billion), as revenue soared 150.3 billion yuan.
Both figures were up sharply as chip demand soars. For the last fiscal year, CXMT reported a net loss of 2.3 billion yuan and revenue of 15.4 billion yuan.
The results could extend CXMT's stellar start to life as a public company. Shares surged 466% on their trading debut in Shanghai a month ago and have continued to rack up gains since then.
As of Friday's close, the company had a total market capitalization of 3.28 trillion yuan-making it China's largest, ahead of the likes of videogame giant Tencent and online retailer Alibaba.

The surge in revenue comes amid a surge in demand for high-speed memory chips, which are needed to process data for AI. Rivals Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung have also racked up significant gains over the past year.
